record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given a finite poset Q and a finite poset P, is there a fixed-parameter algorithm parameterized by P that decides whether P is a chain minor of Q, that is, whether there exists a partial mapping from the ground set of Q to the ground set of P such that every chain of P is the image of some chain of Q under that mapping?

evidence.quote: Question: Is P a chain minor of Q?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let P and Q be finite posets. Say that P is a chain minor of Q if there exists a partial mapping f from the ground set of Q to the ground set of P such that for every chain C of P there is a chain C_Q of Q with f restricted to C_Q being an order-isomorphism onto C. Decide, for input posets P and Q, whether P is a chain minor of Q. The question is whether this problem is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by |P|: does there exist a computable function g and a constant c such that the problem can be solved in time g(|P|) · |Q|^c?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been solved. Blasiak and Durand (arXiv:1304.5849, "Chain minors are FPT", 2013) gave an algorithm deciding whether P is a chain minor of Q that runs in time O(|Q| log |Q|) for every fixed P, thereby establishing fixed-parameter tractability and answering the Downey–Fellows open problem affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Chain minors are FPT
status_evidence.snippet: We give an algorithm that decides whether P is a chain minor of Q in time O(|Q| log |Q|) for every fixed poset P, solving an open problem from the monograph by Downey and Fellows.
status_evidence.claim: The chain minor problem is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by P.

status_evidence.title: Chain Minors Are FPT (Springer)
status_evidence.snippet: Chain Minors Are FPT — chapter establishing FPT status of the chain minor problem.
status_evidence.claim: Published version confirms FPT status of chain minor containment.
